root_cause: Escape key handling in submenus incorrectly closes all submenus via rootMenu.closeChildren() instead of closing only the current submenu.
repair_strategy: Replace the Escape case in the submenu keyup handler to close the current submenu using its controller and focus the controller's toggle element.
expected_accessibility_effect: Escape will close only the innermost open submenu and return focus to its parent menu item, keeping parent submenus open as expected.
functional_risks: If a submenu somehow lacks a controller, the close operation will be skipped (no error).
Focusing the toggle element may not scroll into view if the container overflows, but this matches the original behavior for menu items.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Escape on #history results in focus on #facts, aria-expanded facts=false, aria-expanded about=true.
Verify that Escape on a top-level menubar item still closes the menubar and focuses the controller.
Verify that Escape on a submenu item that has its own submenu (e.g., #overview if it had a submenu) correctly closes that submenu and focuses the parent item.
